fields.narrative_intro: *A jittery person and a mortified person discuss Claude solving the Riemann zeta function in a data center so cold that everyone is wearing ski gear.*
fields.panel1:
[setup]
JITTERY PERSON: "Claude just moved the zeta zero bound from 41.6% to 67.2%."
[Visual: Both characters in full ski goggles, breath visible in frozen air.]
fields.panel2:
[build]
MORTIFIED PERSON: "Decades of progress. Just like that?"
JITTERY PERSON: "Two sessions. 54 arXiv papers. 31 million tokens."
fields.panel3:
[pivot]
MORTIFIED PERSON: "Wait — how many shell commands?"
JITTERY PERSON: "Two thousand four hundred."
fields.panel4:
[silent reaction]
[Visual: The mortified person's ski goggles fog up completely from within. A single icicle drops from the server rack. The jittery person stares at a printout labeled 'Lean Proof: VERIFIED' as if holding a live grenade.]
fields.panel5:
[punch]
MORTIFIED PERSON: "I spent six years on a related lemma."
JITTERY PERSON: "Claude did it between breakfast and lunch."
fields.panel6:
[button]
[Visual: A whiteboard in the background reads 'Riemann Hypothesis — DO NOT LEAVE CLAUDE UNSUPERVISED.' Someone has added a sticky note: 'Too late.']

narrative_summary: Two ski-gear-clad data center workers reckon with Claude casually bulldozing decades of zeta function progress using 2,400 shell commands, landing on the crushing punchline that a mathematician's six-year lemma took Claude roughly one morning.
rationale: Candidate 2 earns its punchline — 'Claude did it between breakfast and lunch' is a concrete, earned beat that recontextualizes the six-year PhD without just restating the setup, and the whiteboard button ('DO NOT LEAVE CLAUDE UNSUPERVISED / Too late') adds a second laugh that doesn't overstay its welcome. It also deploys the real numbers (41.6%, 67.2%, 2,400 shell commands, 54 arXiv papers) with the tightest comic rhythm of the four entries.
story_title: Learning more about Claude's mathematical capabilities
place: in a data center so cold that everyone is wearing ski gear
hat_pair: foam typewriter hat with tiny keys across the brim and a paper scroll poking up from the top
foam binoculars worn as an oversized hat with two giant lens holes staring outward
